summary: Binomial logistic regression (logit link) for next-month credit-card default. The script reads the raw CSV, lower-cases the column names (after read.csv has already converted 'default payment next month' to 'default.payment.next.month' via check.names), drops id, and merges undocumented education codes {0,4,5,6} into 4 and marriage 0 into 3. It merges repayment-status codes {-2,-1,0} into 0 for the six pay_* columns, which the loop addresses by position (6..11). sex, education, marriage and the response become factors. The data is split 70/30 with caret::createDataPartition, stratified on the response, and an 11-variable GLM is fitted on the training rows. 15 coefficients, treatment contrasts, reference levels sex=1, education=1, marriage=1.

preprocessing.description: Read the raw CSV. check.names=TRUE (default) applies make.names, so 'default payment next month' becomes 'default.payment.next.month'. Other headers are already valid names.
Lower-case every column name (ID->id, LIMIT_BAL->limit_bal, PAY_0->pay_0, ...).
Drop the id column. This shifts column positions: limit_bal=1, sex=2, education=3, marriage=4, age=5, pay_0=6, pay_2=7, pay_3=8, pay_4=9, pay_5=10, pay_6=11.
Merge undocumented education codes 0, 5, 6 and 'others' 4 into 4.
For columns at 1-based positions 6..11 AFTER the id drop, i.e. pay_0, pay_2, pay_3, pay_4, pay_5, pay_6, set values in {-2,-1,0} to 0. The columns stay numeric.

preprocessing.r_code: raw.credit$sex <- as.factor(raw.credit$sex); raw.credit$education <- as.factor(...); raw.credit$marriage <- as.factor(...)
preprocessing.description: Convert to factors. The levels are the sorted unique numeric codes: sex {1,2}, education {1,2,3,4}, marriage {1,2,3}. The first level is the reference.
Factor response with levels {0,1}. glm models P(level '1').

preprocessing.r_code: intraining <- createDataPartition(y=..., p=0.7, list=F); train.batch <- raw.credit[intraining,]; test.batch <- raw.credit[-intraining,]
preprocessing.description: Random stratified 70/30 split. No set.seed in the source, so it is not reproducible. The harness captures the membership; Python must import it.

Unpenalised binomial GLM, logit link, fitted by stats::glm.fit IRLS with default glm.control (epsilon=1e-8 on |dev-dev_old|/(|dev|+0.1), maxit=25; the capture reports 6 iterations, converged). summary.glm standard errors come from the QR of the last iteration's weighted design, so R-EST-02 requires reproducing this numerical path, not converging further.
Predicted probability of default on the test rows.

model.formula: default.payment.next.month ~ limit_bal + sex + education + marriage + pay_0 + pay_2 + pay_3 + pay_5 + pay_6 + pay_amt1 + pay_amt2

randomness: caret::createDataPartition (stratified sampling on the response). The source has no set.seed; the capture harness fixed seed 2026 and exported row membership. Python must not resample (R-RNG-01).
risks: Sex and marital status are direct model inputs (Equality Act 2010 protected characteristics). Migrated faithfully per GOV-01; must be assessed in validation.
Undocumented codes (education 0/5/6, marriage 0) are merged into 'others'. A resulting coefficient (education4) may reflect a data artefact.
Merging repayment codes -2/-1/0 is an author assumption, not part of the data definition.
The positional loop seq(6,11) depends on the column order after id is dropped. Any upstream column change silently recodes the wrong variables.
The source has no random seed, so the original split and coefficients cannot be reproduced.
Repayment-status columns are fitted as linear numeric terms even though they are ordinal.
